**My thinking:**

I've been working this land for 30 years. I know this soil. Quzhou gets dry winters and hot summers, and with well irrigation I can manage, but I don't waste water — electricity for the pump costs money. My son works in the city now, so I have less help than before. I have to be practical about labor.

My 15 mu is split the way I've always done it: 10 mu runs wheat in the winter then maize after harvest — that rotation keeps the land healthy and gives me two incomes from the same field. The other 5 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton prices have been soft but I know how to grow it and it fills the summer cash gap differently than grain.

For wheat, I'll use improved seed from the county supply station — I've used Jimai varieties for years, no reason to change. I put down base fertilizer before sowing, top-dress at jointing. I'll irrigate four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and at grain fill. Aphids and powdery mildew always show up, so two to three pesticide passes. Rotary tillage after maize harvest, like always.

For summer maize, I go hybrid — everyone around here does now and the yields are better. Less irrigation needed since July gets some rain, but I'll pump twice more to be safe. Direct seeding after wheat, no-till to save time and effort with less help at home.

Cotton is the most work — that's the truth. I'll use hybrid BT cotton seed. More fertilizer, more irrigation, and I spray more often for bollworm and aphids. I plough deeper for cotton, the roots need it. My daughter-in-law helps during picking season.
